statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is 7% in the low band roughly five and a half hours into the Globex session, with NQ holding a two-sided 226-point range and crude breaking to fresh session lows.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow evidence-based danger window is flagged over 13:00-15:00 UTC, the window containing Monday's US cash open, where an opening-auction imbalance can extend before it retraces. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ holds 30,096.25 (+0.60%) inside a 226-point two-sided range while live WTI breaks to $93.93 and Brent slips under $100; Tail steady at 7%, Stress eases to 32%
body:
Roughly five and a half hours into the Globex session the price path remains two-sided. NQ prints 30,096.25 on Yahoo, up 179.00 points (+0.60%) against the 29,917.25 Friday settle, inside an observed 29,904.50-30,130.50 range, and Investing.com shows 30,098.00 at the same 03:16 UTC stamp - two feeds within 1.75 points. The index sits about 34 points below its session high, having been 51 points below it an hour earlier. So the retracement observed last hour has been partly recovered without a new high being set: price has moved away from the extreme and back toward it, which is exactly the two-sided behaviour this Tail measure is defined against. The full excursion still spans only 0.75%. Tail therefore holds at 7% rather than falling further, because a partial recovery toward the high is a mild extension, and rather than rising, because no retracement has failed.

The energy complex is the material change this hour, and it required correcting the level carried in earlier runs. Trading Economics still shows WTI near $98.00 and Brent near $101.64, but its page timestamps lag - the same page dates its 10-year yield to 18 September. Two independent live sources disagree with it: Yahoo's CL=F front-month contract prints $93.93, down 2.24%, inside a $93.58-$97.03 session range, and FXStreet reported WTI around $93.60 in Asian hours on Monday. Brent on BZ=F prints $97.52, down 1.78%, inside $96.98-$100.26. Crude has therefore fallen about four dollars below the level the previous hours carried, and Brent has broken below $100 for the first time in this decline sequence. Crude making session lows while NQ holds near session highs is a disinflationary, risk-positive alignment; it weakens rather than strengthens the geopolitical transmission channel into equities.

The diplomatic branch driving that move firmed further overnight. Gulf News reported at 03:28 UTC that Trump said he would 'probably be open' to meeting Iranian President Pezeshkian at the UN General Assembly this week, while Tehran has conveyed conditions through Qatari mediators covering an end to fighting on all fronts, release of frozen assets and lifting of the naval blockade. CBS reported that crude, cargo and LNG volumes through the Strait of Hormuz over the past fortnight are the highest in six months, though still below prewar levels. Against that sit verified escalation reports - an intercepted Houthi ballistic-missile attempt on Riyadh, the first on the Saudi capital in this phase, plus thwarted attempts at Yanbu, Taif, Baysh and Farasan. A complex that keeps selling into those headlines is pricing the diplomatic branch, so the escalation is carried as Stress and headline-gap risk, not as an established Tail path.

The rate backdrop is unchanged and remains the heaviest standing weight. The FOMC raised rates 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September, its first hike in three years, and signalled at least one more this year. The 10-year sits at 5.00% and the 2-year at 4.75% as of the 18 September close; the latest H.15 observation, dated 17 September, reads 4.94% and 4.67%. Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is still too high in all aspects of the economy, widely in services and beyond oil, echoing Chair Warsh, who put August PCE near 3.6% at his press conference. VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08%, a calm reading against that backdrop, and is static while the cash market is shut. The cash reference is Friday's NDX close at 29,644.17, up 0.67%, set inside 29,371.89-29,647.80 in a tape where the S&P 500 added 0.17% and the Dow shed 0.18% - split internals rather than aligned ones.

Two session-structure points shape the hours ahead. Tokyo is closed today for Respect for the Aged Day, so Asian liquidity is thinner than a normal Monday; thin books make individual prints erratic without making them directional. And the week's principal catalyst advanced another stage: Bessent and Greer met Vice Premier He Lifeng and Li Chenggang in New York on Sunday for roughly eight hours on AI, tariffs and critical minerals, Bessent called the talks very successful, the US proposed a US-China AI dialogue with an incident notification mechanism, and a working group is reported to continue on Monday. No announcements were made on advanced-chip export controls or critical-minerals supply. The Trump-Xi summit is confirmed for 24 September in Washington. A preparatory round that concludes constructively and continues narrows dispersion into the summit rather than widening it. Monday's own calendar is light: Goolsbee at 10:30 UTC, the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30 UTC and bill auctions at 15:30 UTC.

The shared Finviz context for this run is again only partial - its futures and calendar sections failed collection - and at roughly three hours old it is well outside the freshness bound, so it is treated as stale and not relied upon. The independent research above stands on its own.

Net: Tail 7%, unchanged, because the path remains two-sided inside a 0.75% range with no failed retracement and no new session high. The mapped state stays EA_ON and green. Stress eases to 32% as crude breaks four dollars lower and Brent clears $100 to the downside, against an unchanged 5.00% 10-year and a Fed that has just resumed hiking. Confidence rises to 79% on two futures feeds agreeing within 1.75 points, live oil and Brent futures that resolved a stale third-party quote, a verified NDX close, a seven-day US calendar re-verified in this run, and multiple independently fetched and verified reports including one published within the last hour; it is discounted for the absence of live cash-market cross-asset confirmation and for Finviz context that is both partial and stale.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available and describe an unbroken low-Tail regime across Sunday 20 September and into the Globex reopen. Tail held between 4% and 9% in every hour, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout. It sat at 5% through the entire weekend halt, then rose with the reopen as the first live price path formed, peaking at 9% in the 01:00 UTC slot before easing to 7% in the most recent hour as the extension unwound. Stress drifted from 25% early on 20 September into a 30-35% band as the post-hike rate backdrop and the elevated oil complex accumulated, easing to 33% in the final hour. Confidence ranged from 70% to 78%, dipping in the deepest part of the halt when no live price path existed and recovering once futures reopened and two feeds could be cross-checked. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours. The present assessment holds Tail steady at 7% for a second hour.
outlookSummary: The cycle covers the remainder of the Asian session, the European session, the Monday US cash session through the 20:00 UTC close, the CME maintenance halt and the Tuesday Globex reopen. Tail is projected to stay inside the low band in all 24 hours, so the mapped policy state remains EA_ON throughout. The projected peak is 12% in the hour containing the 13:30 UTC US cash open, followed by 11% in the hour after it, which is why the flagged danger window spans 13:00-15:00 UTC; secondary 10% readings fall on the 12:30 UTC Chicago Fed release, the 15:30 UTC bill auctions and power hour into the 20:00 UTC close. The cycle low of 6% falls in the 21:00-22:00 UTC maintenance halt, when no NQ price path exists and a no-retracement trend is mechanically impossible. Stress is projected between 31% and 37%, held up by a 5.00% 10-year and a Fed that has just resumed hiking, and capped by crude at fresh session lows and a constructive US-China preparatory round that continues on Monday. Confidence decays from 79% to 68% across the cycle as the evidence base ages. These are conditional projections: no future price-path structure is treated as already observed, and an upgrade would require observed shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after failed retracements.
